about.description:
Enumlib.jl generates the derivative superstructures of a parent lattice,
including multilattices such as HCP, over all concentrations or a restricted
concentration range. It is a from-scratch Julia reimplementation of enumlib by
one of its original authors, and a drop-in replacement for the Fortran enum.x:
the struct_enum.in / struct_enum.out file contract is unchanged.

This package provides the enum.x, polya.x and makestr.x executables, compiled
ahead of time with a bundled Julia system image, so no Julia installation is
required to run them.

raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "0.4.0"

package:
  name: enumlib.jl
  version: ${{ version }}

# Built from source, not repackaged from a release artifact: conda-forge asked for
# the application to be compiled in the recipe (staged-recipes#34550).
source:
  url: https://github.com/glwhart/Enumlib.jl/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 2b2ffd05f93e4c2af831633f69d5d64780dccbec578b005cbae3516b7789789b

build:
  number: 0
  # The platforms conda-forge ships a `julia` package for AND builds natively.
  #
  # osx-arm64 is absent for a structural reason, not a missing dependency:
  # conda-forge cross-compiles osx-arm64 on osx-64 runners, but
  # PackageCompiler.create_app has to execute target-architecture code to
  # precompile its system image, and a Julia system image cannot be
  # cross-compiled. So no arm64 Julia package would help here either. Under
  # discussion on the PR; Apple Silicon users have native arm64 binaries on the
  # project's GitHub releases in the meantime.
  skip:
    - win
    - linux and not x86_64
    - osx and arm64
  script:
    file: build.sh

requirements:
  build:
    # PackageCompiler links the app's launchers with a C compiler.
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
  host:
    # julia is in `host`, not `build`, on purpose. create_app copies Julia's
    # runtime libraries into the application, and those copies carry references
    # to wherever they came from -- so they have to come from $PREFIX, which
    # conda-build relocates, rather than $BUILD_PREFIX, which it does not.
    # build.sh calls $PREFIX/bin/julia by explicit path rather than trusting PATH.
    #
    # 1.10.4 is too old (a dependency floors at 1.11.6) and conda-forge packages
    # no 1.11, so 1.12 it is. The upstream test suite passes on 1.12.7.
    - julia 1.12.*
    # conda-forge's julia deliberately strips Julia's vendored libraries
    # (see its build.sh: rm $PREFIX/lib/julia/{libcholmod,libcurl,libssh2,
    # libgit2,libssl}.so) and links against these instead. An application built
    # with it inherits them as runtime dependencies rather than bundling them,
    # so the run requirements come from these entries' run_exports.
    #
    # This mirrors julia-feedstock's own host list. It is deliberately generous
    # for a first build -- conda-build's overlinking check will report what the
    # application actually links, and this should be trimmed to that.
    - openblas-ilp64
    - openlibm
    - gmp
    - mpfr
    - curl
    - libssh2
    - if: not osx
      then: libgit2
    - if: linux
      then: libunwind
    - if: osx
      then: libosxunwind
    - arpack
    - suitesparse
    - pcre2
    - libutf8proc
    - libnghttp2
    - zlib
  run:
    # Explicit rather than left to the host entries' run_exports, because the
    # test environment proved those insufficient: the application failed with
    #
    #   Unable to load dependent library
    #     $PREFIX/libexec/enumlib.jl/bin/../lib/julia/libopenlibm.so
    #
    # The application links these out of $PREFIX/lib rather than bundling copies,
    # so each one has to be present at run time. openlibm, for instance, exports
    # nothing, so nothing was adding it. The list is what the build's own linking
    # pass resolved -- libutf8proc, libunwind and the whole SuiteSparse and
    # BLAS/LAPACK chain -- plus the rest of the host set that julia links.
    - openblas-ilp64
    - libblas
    - liblapack
    - openlibm
    - gmp
    - mpfr
    - curl
    - libssh2
    - if: not osx
      then: libgit2
    - if: linux
      then: libunwind
    - if: osx
      then: libosxunwind
    - arpack
    - suitesparse
    - pcre2
    - libutf8proc
    - libnghttp2
    - zlib

tests:
  - script:
      # Engine identification. Downstream tools (pymatgen's EnumlibAdaptor) probe
      # this exact token to tell the Julia engine from the legacy Fortran enum.x.
      - enum.x --version
      - polya.x --version
      - makestr.x --version
      - enum.x --version | grep "Enumlib.jl"
      # Enumerate, count, and generate structures, using the same invocation style
      # the Fortran enumlib feedstock tests with: input file as a positional arg.
      - enum.x struct_enum.in.fcc
      - test -f struct_enum.out
      - polya.x struct_enum.in.fcc
      - makestr.x struct_enum.out 1 1
      - test -f vasp.1
    files:
      recipe:
        - struct_enum.in.fcc

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/glwhart/Enumlib.jl
  summary: Derivative-structure enumeration (Julia reimplementation of enumlib)
  description: |
    Enumlib.jl generates the derivative superstructures of a parent lattice,
    including multilattices such as HCP, over all concentrations or a restricted
    concentration range. It is a from-scratch Julia reimplementation of enumlib by
    one of its original authors, and a drop-in replacement for the Fortran enum.x:
    the struct_enum.in / struct_enum.out file contract is unchanged.

    This package provides the enum.x, polya.x and makestr.x executables, compiled
    ahead of time with a bundled Julia system image, so no Julia installation is
    required to run them.
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  documentation: https://glwhart.github.io/Enumlib.jl
  repository: https://github.com/glwhart/Enumlib.jl

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - glwhart
